children: OTTAWA--The Bank of Canada on Wednesday left its main interest rate unchanged at 2.25%.

The move was widely expected, according to a Wall Street Journal survey of economists last week, as policymakers take a wait-and-see approach as the economy deals with an escalation in the U.S.-Canada trade conflict, and the risk that elevated energy prices push up prices for other goods

The fraying of economic and diplomatic ties between the neighboring countries poses yet another headwind for Canada, which recent data indicated had perhaps turned the corner after a trade-uncertainty-induced period of stagnant activity.

The Bank of Canada leaving its policy rate on hold "is less an indication that the current policy rate is right, and more a sign that it is not clear that the current policy rate is incorrect," said David Watt, a former economist at HSBC and author of a Canadian economics newsletter. "Sometimes, if you are not sure which direction to go, it's best to sit still."
